name: First Class
description: First Class completes the foundational outdoor skills: menu planning and serving as cook, lashings, orienteering and GPS, plants and weather, boating safety, advanced first aid, home emergency planning, citizenship and recruiting.

provenance.notes: Topic outline drafted from maintainer familiarity with the Scouts BSA rank requirements (the structure introduced in 2016 and revised since) and cross-referenced with secondary sources found by web search. Official rank requirements could not be reached from the build environment. Several sub-requirements under 1, 6 and 9 are not yet transcribed.

references.label: Wikipedia: Ranks in Scouts BSA (secondary source)

requirements.title: Outdoor activities and ethics
requirements.summary: Taking part in the required troop activities, including overnight campouts, and outdoor ethics.
requirements.note: Sub-requirements are not yet transcribed in this outline.

requirements.title: Menu planning and camp cooking
requirements.summary: Planning a menu and budget, choosing gear, handling perishable food safely, and serving as patrol cook.

children.title: Planning a menu
children.summary: Helping plan a menu for a campout that meets nutritional needs.

children.title: Budget and amounts
children.summary: Making a shopping list with a budget and the food amounts needed.

children.title: Cooking gear
children.summary: Showing which pans, utensils and gear the menu needs.

children.title: Safe food handling
children.summary: Safe handling and storage of meat, dairy, eggs, vegetables and other perishable food.
children.orientation: The USDA danger zone is 40–140 °F, where bacteria grow fastest. On a trip, that means keeping cold foods cold, not leaving perishables out too long (less time in hot weather), and cooking to safe internal temperatures checked with a food thermometer rather than by color.

children.title: Serving as cook
children.summary: Serving as cook on a campout and supervising helpers.

requirements.title: Lashings
requirements.summary: When to use lashings, the knots that start and finish them, and using lashings to build something useful.

children.title: When to use lashings
children.summary: When you should and should not use lashings.

children.title: Timber hitch and clove hitch
children.summary: Tying the timber hitch and clove hitch.

children.title: Basic lashings
children.summary: Tying square, shear and diagonal lashings.

children.title: A camp gadget
children.summary: Using lashings to build a useful camp gadget or structure.

requirements.title: Navigation
requirements.summary: Completing an orienteering course and using an electronic navigation tool.

children.title: Orienteering course
children.summary: Completing an orienteering course with map and compass.

children.title: GPS and electronic navigation
children.summary: Using a GPS unit, phone app or other electronic navigation system.

requirements.title: Nature and weather
requirements.summary: Identifying native plants, getting weather forecasts, reading natural signs of hazardous weather, and preparing for extreme weather.

children.title: Native plants
children.summary: Identifying or showing evidence of native plants in your area.

children.title: Weather forecasts
children.summary: Ways to get a weather forecast and why forecasts matter when planning an activity.
children.orientation: The National Weather Service is the primary public source of U.S. forecasts and warnings. Learn the difference between a watch (conditions are favorable) and a warning (the hazard is happening or imminent), and decide ahead of time what each would mean for your trip.

children.title: Natural signs of hazardous weather
children.summary: Natural indicators that dangerous weather is approaching and what to do about it.
children.orientation: Building cumulus clouds, a sudden drop in temperature, rising wind and distant thunder are all signs to act early. Thunder means lightning is within striking distance, so move to safe shelter right away and wait until 30 minutes after the last thunder.

children.title: Extreme weather where you live
children.summary: Extreme weather you might meet in your area and how to plan for it.

requirements.title: Swimming and boating
requirements.summary: The swimmer test, safe trips afloat, boat parts, and line rescues.
requirements.note: Sub-requirements are not yet transcribed in this outline.

requirements.title: First aid and emergency preparedness
requirements.summary: Bandaging, moving injured people, heart attack signs and CPR, home utilities, a home emergency plan and safe water in an emergency.

children.title: Bandages
children.summary: Applying bandages for several injuries, such as a sprained ankle and head and arm injuries.

children.title: Moving an injured person
children.summary: Moving a person from a hazardous room and helping someone with a sprained ankle to safety.

children.title: Heart attack and CPR
children.summary: The common signs of a heart attack and the steps of CPR.

children.title: Home utilities
children.summary: The utility services in your home or meeting place, their hazards, and emergency responses.

children.title: Home emergency plan
children.summary: Developing an emergency action plan for your home covering fire, storms and outages.
children.orientation: A home emergency plan covers who to contact, where to meet, how to get out, and what to do when the power or water is off. Ready.gov’s family planning guide walks through the pieces and has printable templates.

children.title: Safe water in an emergency
children.summary: How to get safe drinking water in an emergency.

requirements.title: Fitness
requirements.summary: Continuing regular physical activity and reflecting on your progress.

requirements.title: Citizenship and environment
requirements.summary: Constitutional rights and obligations, a local environmental issue, reducing trash, and service.
requirements.note: Sub-requirements are not yet transcribed in this outline.

requirements.title: Sharing Scouting
requirements.summary: Telling someone eligible about Scouting and inviting them to an activity.

requirements.title: Scout spirit
requirements.summary: Showing Scout spirit by living the Scout Oath and Scout Law.

requirements.title: Scoutmaster conference
requirements.summary: Taking part in a Scoutmaster conference.

requirements.title: Board of review
requirements.summary: Completing a board of review for the rank.
